1.tldr: I'm a Gonzaga DPLS doctoral student spending a semester at West University of Timișoara on Erasmus+. This blog is my reflection practice, mixing practical travel notes with thinking about leadership and identity.

3.summary_title: A Year in the Making: Saying Yes to Romania
3.tldr: The backstory of applying to Erasmus a year earlier, while one part of my brain kept asking "who do I think I am?" It ends on the eve of departure, excited and uneasy about a season of not being the expert.

33.tldr: The hardest part of leaving was my family, not the luggage, including a week of trying to turn "mom" into a checklist. A layover in Amsterdam dropped me into a Lunar New Year celebration that felt like permission to be delighted.

59.tldr: Arriving in Timișoara brought travel fog, the humility of the language barrier, and an airport that reminded me of Saipan. The dorm was a shock: not cozy, not home, and up several flights of stairs with 130 pounds of luggage.

122.tldr: I turned panic into a shopping checklist and learned that "walkable" means something different in Romania. By the end the room felt livable and I felt capable, if not settled.

165.tldr: A coffee shop by the dorm became my daily office, where 8 a.m. counts as early and nobody asks you to leave after seven hours. How the café treats time became a way to read how the culture treats space and pace.

178.tldr: A practical primer on Romanian restaurant norms, starting with the fact that you seat yourself. A surprise plate of chicken liver pâté confirmed the universe's insistence that I eat liver.

208.summary_title: It's not you, it's the culture
208.tldr: American small talk with cashiers and drivers gets baffled looks, because friendliness with strangers can read as intrusion here. My accent gives me away instantly, and daily corrections from servers became my language practice.

215.summary_title: The Coolest in the Parking Lot
215.tldr: I assumed "DUB (ENG)" on a movie listing meant dubbed in English and sat through 100 minutes of the animated film GOAT in un-subtitled Romanian. I still cried at the ending, and decided humility is sometimes the price of a ticket.

246.summary_title: Corvin Castle: And the Problem with Dracula
246.tldr: Corvin Castle, with its Gothic towers and moat, looks more like Dracula's castle than Bran does. It sets the castle up as a place where stories live and opens the Hunedoara cluster.

288.summary_title: Stories of Romania: [The Well of the Three Prisoners]
288.tldr: A retold legend of three Ottoman prisoners promised freedom by John Hunyadi if they dug a well through solid rock. Whether the story is true is left open, but someone did dig that well.

304.tldr: A comic account of uneven medieval staircases and what they do to modern calves. The view from the top made it worth it.

341.summary_title: Stories of Romania [The Raven of Corvin Castle]
341.tldr: A folktale about King Sigismund, a village woman, a ring, and a raven, explaining John Hunyadi's origins and his raven coat of arms. It ends where Hunyadi's own story begins.

351.summary_title: Chronicles of Romania [John Hunyadi and Matthias Corvinus]
351.tldr: A short history of Hunyadi's wins against the Ottomans and his son Matthias's reign as a reforming, book-collecting king. My favorite fact is Hunyadi's contemporary nickname, "Turk-buster."

376.summary_title: Chronicles of Romania [Vlad III of Wallachia: Monster, Myth, Man]
376.tldr: A sourced look at Vlad the Impaler as Western horror icon, Romanian defender, and one brutal ruler in a brutal century. It asks why the same violence gets remembered so differently.

417.summary_title: The Rhythm of a Small City
417.tldr: A café-table sketch of Hunedoara in early spring, slower and quieter than Timișoara. Before tourist season the town still belongs to the people who live there.

438.tldr: A visit to Hunedoara's small Communism Museum, past factory gates 20,000 workers once crossed daily. Objects from the years I was a kid watching She-Ra made this history feel closer than the castle's.

471.summary_title: Field Notes: Paper, Ink and Identity
471.tldr: The museum's room of banknotes seemed out of place until I started reading money as a country's self-portrait. Mostly a captioned photo essay.

520.summary_title: Field Notes: Tiny Worlds in Hunedoara
520.tldr: A miniature train museum I found while video-calling Jason, who loves model trains. It turned into a reflection on hobbies as part of a life's story and a way to remember someone.

533.tldr: I followed church bells into an Orthodox service already underway and stood at the back trying not to intrude. A few minutes of chant and incense felt like stepping into another world.

548.tldr: A wrap-up arguing the castle is only one layer of the town, alongside communist-era ruins, the promenade, and small museums. Staying put let the town become more than its headline attraction.

564.tldr: Red-and-white charms appeared all over the city for March 1, and I learned the tradition behind them. The image I kept is an older man carefully pinning one to his partner's coat.

574.tldr: Overlapping versions of the Baba Dochia and Dragobete legends tied to the arrival of spring. It closes with a list of Romanian idioms and their literal translations.

586.tldr: Flower stalls took over every corner around March 8 as people bought tulips for the women in their lives. Like Mărțișor, a month built from small gestures.

598.tldr: My overnight train trip started with a misread ticket, a wandering Uber, and a sprint to the station. The train had been delayed all day, so the urgency was real but the problem wasn't.

599.tldr: A history primer on how Romania came under communist rule and how ordinary people got by. It frames Romania as a country that absorbs change without disappearing.

609.tldr: Why so many grand houses in "Little Paris" sit derelict, tracing it back to communist nationalization of private property. Through broken windows you can still see the fireplaces and crown moldings.

631.summary_title: Field Notes: Bucharest – Crisis Creates Opportunities… [But for who?]
631.tldr: The 1977 earthquake gave the regime cover to bulldoze neighborhoods, which made me rethink a phrase I have leaned on for years in crisis work. Crisis doesn't decide what gets built or erased, people do.

651.summary_title: Field Notes: Time for a spa day!
651.tldr: Fourteen hours at a huge Bucharest thermal spa, saunas and red-light beds included. The highlight was a sauna ritual involving icy birch branches I did not knowingly sign up for.

680.tldr: For the first time I traveled without my usual color-coded Plan, arriving with one goal: see the white horses. Meet the planned version of me, who would have been efficient and missed things.

708.summary_title: Vienna: Dancing White Horses and Chandeliers
708.tldr: Watching a Lipizzaner training session at the Spanish Riding School in the Hofburg. The horses' visible mistakes and years of repetition handed me a lesson I give others and rarely apply to myself.

734.tldr: Over coffee after the show, strangers told me how the Lipizzaners nearly disappeared in WWII. It connects to pentimento, the art term at the center of my leadership research.

747.summary_title: Stories of Vienna: Once Upon a War
747.tldr: A fairy-tale retelling of how the Third Reich gathered the Lipizzaners and Polish Arabians to breed a "master race" of horses, and how they were saved. It ends with Polish horsemen rebuilding their breed from a few dozen survivors.

767.tldr: Hungry on Easter Sunday with no cash and a confused GPS, I ended up in a restaurant built on Roman ruins and had one of the best meals of my life. The planned version of me would have had a good trip and missed it.

771.tldr: Partway through the Belvedere I stopped looking at the art and started watching how people react to it. Then I went back to the entrance and walked the whole museum again.

820.summary_title: Vienna: The Kiss and the Checkpoint
820.tldr: The longest Vienna post: finally seeing Klimt's The Kiss in a crowd focused on getting the photo. It asks how museum design rewards documentation over encounter.

873.tldr: On the Belvedere's quiet top floor, with less glass between me and the art, I thought about why famous paintings now sit behind protective glass after activist attacks. Something was lost, and I was lucky to see it before.

884.tldr: Flying in instead of taking the train was a mistake, but the city surprised me. A trumpet call that keeps cutting off mid-note sets up a story for later.

926.summary_title: Krakow: The Accidental Private Food Tour
926.tldr: A group food tour cancels and becomes a one-on-one with guide Jason, a Portland transplant who came to help Ukrainian refugees and stayed. It ends with more vodka than planned and a classical concert next door.

944.summary_title: Stories of Krakow: The Dragon, The Bugler, The Enchanted Knights
944.tldr: Three Krakow legends: the Wawel dragon, the Saint Mary's bugler whose song breaks off, and knights turned into the pigeons of the market square. Told in the "bajka, nie bajka" (maybe true, maybe not) style.

947.tldr: Washing machines, signs, and insurance offices keep forcing me to stop and orient before acting. Judgment sometimes starts on a street corner, and the schnitzel I ordered turned out to be liver.

964.summary_title: What a Visa Office Taught Me About AI Governance
964.tldr: Three weeks of circular insurance rejections for a visa became a case study in opaque systems with no accountable owner. It draws on my research project "What Frameworks Cannot See."

972.tldr: On the conference's first day I went back to a restaurant from an earlier visit for coccoli con stracchino. Florence holds layers of past versions of me, and I let them sit together.

979.tldr: The series opener: a small conference that felt more like a retreat, held under Raphael's School of Athens. It previews themes of care, power, place, and tradition.

1015.summary_title: The History of Florence Is Full of Women… [If You Know Where to Look]
1015.tldr: Art historian Cristina Bibbiani's tour surfaced the women hidden in Florence's history. Walking home, I wondered what maps I've been missing in other cities.

1069.tldr: Unattributed notes from a panel of accomplished women on voice, legitimacy, and leadership style. The relief was learning that weight I thought was mine alone sits on a lot of shoulders.

1097.tldr: Gonzaga alum Sarah Kinsella's session on "those who can, must" and not confusing exhaustion with seriousness. Living well is part of how the work gets done, not a reward afterward.

1117.tldr: In Denise Hossom's care-ethics workshop, my page stayed nearly empty while everyone else's filled up. Receiving care, it turns out, is the harder part for me.

1133.tldr: A short prose poem, inspired by Carolotta Ferrari's story, about a mother held up by a network of women across the city. Written differently from the rest of the notes.

1142.summary_title: A Global City at Human Scale
1142.tldr: A slow, loud group dinner on the first night shows how trust needs unhurried time. Real influence starts with people who have time to know each other.

1165.tldr: Repeat visits to the Accademia and David lead to the question of what wealth and patronage owe the future. Powerful people leave fingerprints, and some become wounds, some beauty, some both.

1201.tldr: A visit to Florence's leather school, shadowed by the recent death of Tommaso Melani. It contrasts inherited craft with Francesca Gori's bags, which make history vivid instead of embalming it.

1231.summary_title: What Is in a Bottle of Wine?
1231.tldr: I barely drink wine, but at Antinori nel Chianti Classico I was captivated by people explaining what they love. Inheritance, stewardship, and tradition versus innovation in a centuries-old family business.

1275.tldr: A Turda weekend for the salt mine and a spa (the "Luca version" of the trip, after an imaginary Instagram travel bro) turned into an unplanned mountain hike, a broken hammam, and a lot of butterflies. A story worth having anyway.

1333.tldr: The trip home: a missed bus, an overpriced taxi, a sweltering city bus to Cluj, a surprise fancy hotel, and a late train. The plan failed, but the view of shepherds and their flocks did not.

1362.tldr: Short portraits of people from the semester: the librarian who was my first friend, a teacher, a taxi driver, coffee-shop regulars, and "Luca." I circled the word "earnestness" to come back to later.

1375.tldr: Months of immigration-office visits with no status updates or progress bar. My Romanian test phrase finally fits: "I must wait" for a residence card that already exists somewhere in the building.

1389.tldr: Bran Castle turns out to be several castles at once: the Dracula souvenir economy, Queen Marie's home, the folklore, and Vlad's. A bookend to the Corvin Castle post, ending on hearts carved into doors.
